after.worked_solution:
First, let's factor out $-4$ from the expression. We have

$$
-100-36{m}^{2}=-4(25+9{m}^{2}).
$$

Let's now focus on factoring the expression $(25+9{m}^{2}).$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}25+9{m}^{2} & =25-(-9{m}^{2}) \\  & =25-(9{\text{i}}^{2}{m}^{2}) \\  & ={5}^{2}-{(3\text{i}m)}^{2} \\  & =(5+3\text{i}m)(5-3\text{i}m)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into the expression, we get

$$
-4(25+9{m}^{2})=-4(5+3\text{i}m)(5-3\text{i}m).
$$

The expression −100−36m2 is equivalent to

a
−(5+3im)(5−3im)
b
−4(5+3im)(5−3im)
c
−5(4+3im)(4−3im)
d
−(3+5im)(3−5im)
e
−5(3+4im)(3−4im)

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's factor out −4 from the expression. We have

−100−36m2=−4(25+9m2).

Let's now focus on factoring the expression (25+9m2).

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using i2=−1. Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

25+9m2=25−(−9m2)=25−(9i2m2)=52−(3im)2=(5+3im)(5−3im)

Finally, substituting this back into the expression, we get

−4(25+9m2)=−4(5+3im)(5−3im).

content.worked_solution:
First, let's factor out $-4$ from the expression. We have

$$
-100-36{m}^{2}=-4(25+9{m}^{2}).
$$

Let's now focus on factoring the expression $(25+9{m}^{2}).$

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}25+9{m}^{2} & =25-(-9{m}^{2}) \\  & =25-(9{\text{i}}^{2}{m}^{2}) \\  & ={5}^{2}-{(3\text{i}m)}^{2} \\  & =(5+3\text{i}m)(5-3\text{i}m)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into the expression, we get

$$
-4(25+9{m}^{2})=-4(5+3\text{i}m)(5-3\text{i}m).
$$

$$
{y}^{10}+16={({y}^{5})}^{2}+{4}^{2}.

$$

$$

Question 2

Factor y10+16.

a
(y5+8i)(y5−8i)
b
(y5−8i)2
c
(y10+4)(y10−4)
d
(y5+4i)2
e
(y5+4i)(y5−4i)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the given expression is a sum of squares, since

y10+16=(y5)2+42.

To factor a sum of squares, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using i2=−1. Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

y10+16=y10−(−16)=y10−(16i2)=(y5)2−(4i)2=(y5+4i)(y5−4i)

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{10}+16 & ={y}^{10}-(-16) \\  & ={y}^{10}-(16{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & ={({y}^{5})}^{2}-{(4\text{i})}^{2} \\  & =({y}^{5}+4\text{i})({y}^{5}-4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, let's factor the expression as a perfect square trinomial in ${w}^{2}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}4{w}^{4}+36{w}^{2}+81 & ={(2{w}^{2})}^{2}+2\cdot (2{w}^{2})\cdot 9+{9}^{2} \\  & =(2{w}^{2}+9)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to factor the sum of squares in the parentheses. To do this, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${\text{i}}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}2{w}^{2}+9 & =2{w}^{2}-(-9) \\  & =2{w}^{2}-(9{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & =(\sqrt{2}w)^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2} \\  & =(\sqrt{2}w+3\text{i})(\sqrt{2}w-3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{w}^{4}+36{w}^{2}+81 & =(2{w}^{2}+9)^{2} \\  & =((\sqrt{2}w+3\text{i})(\sqrt{2}w-3\text{i}))^{2} \\  & =(\sqrt{2}w+3\text{i})^{2}(\sqrt{2}w-3\text{i})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
